skill.name: explain-codebase
skill.description: Build an onboarding map of an unfamiliar repository covering purpose, entry points, how to run it, main modules, data flow and risky areas, with file references. Use when asked to explain, map or onboard onto a codebase.
skill.summary: Map an unfamiliar repository with source references, setup commands, a central execution flow, and open questions.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: Eight detections are benign Markdown, read-only history inspection, or protective rules. One low-severity risk remains: repository-defined tests and lint may execute untrusted project code without a trust check. No evidence found of prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories make it difficult to find entry points, setup steps, and important dependencies. This skill guides an assistant through source inspection to create a concise onboarding map with file references.
actual_capabilities: Identify repository purpose and intended users from documentation and package descriptions.
Extract installation, run, and test commands from manifests, Makefiles, and continuous integration configuration.
Map two directory levels, identify languages and frameworks, and locate application entry points.
Trace one central request, command, or event through files and functions to storage or output.
Summarize data models, configuration variable names, and external service dependencies without printing secret values.
Describe tests, quality checks, recent file churn, reading priorities, and unresolved questions with source references.
limitations: Requires repository access and an assistant with suitable file inspection tools.
Produces a concise orientation map, not exhaustive documentation or a complete security audit.
Command verification depends on available dependencies, permissions, and a trusted execution environment.
Cannot verify business context or runtime behavior that the inspected files do not establish.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an Existing Project
use_cases.description: Find setup commands, key modules, and a suggested reading order before making a first contribution.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Technical Handoff
use_cases.description: Summarize responsibilities, service dependencies, and one important execution flow for a receiving team.

use_cases.title: Scope Architecture Questions
use_cases.description: Review entry points, data boundaries, quality signals, and unanswered questions before planning deeper investigation.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads evaluating an unfamiliar repository

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Repository Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this repository for a newcomer. Cover purpose, major directories, entry points, and three files to read first. Cite inspected files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup and Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Find install, run, and test commands from repository configuration. Inspect task definitions before proposing execution. Mark every command as verified or unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Central Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this repository and trace its central request or command from entry to storage or output. List files, functions, configuration names, and service boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Evidence-Based Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise handoff map with one complete flow, test coverage signals, recent churn, and risky areas. Cite evidence, label inference, and list open questions. Obtain approval before running repository tasks.

output_examples.input: Explain a repository when tests cannot run in the current environment.
output: How to run: setup and test commands are identified from project configuration but remain unverified.
Quality signals: test locations and configured checks are documented from inspected files.
Open questions: dependency availability and test results remain unknown.
Data and config: list environment variable names referenced by the application, without their values.
External services: identify integrations supported by inspected code and configuration.
Open questions: service availability and production configuration remain unverified.

best_practices: Inspect repository task definitions and obtain approval before executing commands from an unfamiliar project.
Require source references for factual claims and separate verified observations from inference.
Trace one representative workflow and record unresolved questions instead of guessing.
anti_patterns: Running repository scripts before checking their behavior and the execution environment.
Including secret values from environment files, configuration, or command output.
Treating a short onboarding map as exhaustive documentation or a completed security review.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. Repository inspection requires suitable file access.

faq.question: Does this skill change repository files?
faq.answer: Its instructions focus on inspection and reporting. Suggested test or lint commands can still execute project code and create artifacts.

faq.question: Will it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: The skill asks the assistant to run inexpensive tests and lint checks. Review task definitions and approve execution before using unfamiliar repositories.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to report environment variable names only and never print secret values from environment files or configuration.

faq.question: What does the final report include?
faq.answer: Expect purpose, setup steps, a directory map, one execution flow, configuration, services, reading priorities, risky areas, and open questions.

faq.question: Can it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It identifies orientation risks and quality signals, but it does not provide comprehensive vulnerability analysis or guarantee runtime behavior.
